conclusion:
U-17 is RESOLVED and the handoff's 'No notice found' is wrong. CME Globex Notice ran the item 'TACO and BTIC Amended Trading Schedule' on 2021-09-06, 2021-09-13 and 2021-09-20: 'Effective this Sunday, September 26 (trade date Monday, September 27) ... the Basis Trade at Cash Open (“TACO”) and Basis Trade at Index Close (“BTIC”) will open for Monday's trade date on the previous Friday afternoon. With this change and for the first time, CME Globex will support trading for a trade date over a weekend. The trade date for these products will not roll over on the weekend.' The far side of the change is CME's own client-systems wiki, whose page 'Basis Trade at Cash Open' carries its own last-modified stamp Feb 26 2020 in the 2020-07-01 / 2021-06-11 / 2021-06-21 captures (Monday-Thursday) and Oct 11 2021 in the 2021-10-26 / 2022-05-28 captures (Monday-Friday). The ES ContractSpecs Globex TACO cell flips exactly once across 14 archived captures, between 2021-07-03 and 2022-09-08, which contains 2021-09-26. No postponement item appeared in the 2021-09-27, 2021-10-04 or 2021-10-11 notices — CME did flag a postponement for iLink 3 FIXP in those same notices, so its absence here is meaningful.

U-16 is RESOLVED in the sense the handoff needs — the implementer now knows what to encode and why — although CME publishes no prose that EXPLAINS the Saturday rows. Four independent measurements settle it. (1) Census: across 3,243 products the Saturday event signature (05:00 open, 17:00 closed) occurs on exactly five — ESQ, NQQ, RTQ and the two Nikkei BTIC roots NIT and NKT. The crypto complex's Saturday shape is a completely different, separately sourced triple (02:00 closed, 03:45 preopen, 04:00 open) on 265 products, so the 'crypto-style Saturday maintenance' hypothesis is dead. (2) The five are precisely the products carrying a Friday morning open whose tradingDate is the following Monday — i.e. exactly the population the 2021-09-26 'trade date does not roll over on the weekend' change created. (3) The row is byte-identical on TACO (Chicago-anchored: Friday 08:30 close, 09:30 pre-open, 10:00 open) and on Nikkei BTIC (Tokyo-anchored: Friday 01:30 close, 10:30 pre-open, 11:00 open). Two families with different anchors and different Friday legs emitting one identical Saturday row is a shared template row, not a product session. (4) It is invariant where a real session could not be: unchanged across the 2026-11-01 US DST end; unchanged after the early-close Friday 2026-11-27 (12:15 CT); and still present after Friday 2026-12-25, a full holiday whose event list is empty — an 'open' with nothing that opened it, and with no pre-open, unlike every other open in the group's week.

Against that, three CME prose statements say the market is shut over the weekend: SER-8124R Exhibit 1 ('Friday ... No day session. Trading shall resume on Sunday evening.'); the client-systems wiki, era 2 and still live today ('No TACO orders will be persisted over the weekend. Clients must re-enter their Day/session orders for Monday trade date when we re-open Sunday for Monday's trade date.'); and CME's own Taco-Friday-Scenario diagram, whose only markers are Friday, 'Sunday Start' and Monday. So the Saturday events are a trading-hours-service artifact and the weekend is closed.

That forces a narrowing of the handoff's decision rule, and the narrowing is itself sourced. The rule currently counts 'a closed@ event in the trading-hours service' as session language. It has to read: a feed event counts as session language only where no operator prose contradicts it. Here the feed is contradicted three times over by CME's own words, and the crate should follow the prose. Reading the feed literally would have shipped a 12-hour Saturday session on five roots that CME says do not trade at all on Saturday.

U-17's second half (the NQQ/RTQ listing) is answered and is also not a blocker. CME Clearing Advisory 20-061, notice date 2020-02-26, header Effective Date 23 March 2020, tabulates 'Listing Date  Trade Date Monday, March 23, 2020' with both roots and the era-1 Globex grid. Under AGENTS.md ('A member product listing after the family clock began remains caller catalog data unless it changes the family schedule itself') this listing is catalog data — it adds no revision row, so the future-tense 2026 page sentence the handoff worried about never mattered.

One adjudication is handed back rather than made here, because it is not this gate's to make and it is not confined to TACO. All four TACO-relevant dated documents — Globex Notice 2018-05-07, SER-8124R, Clearing Advisory 20-061 and Globex Notice 2021-09-06/13/20 — state their effective day with CME's boilerplate 'pending all relevant CFTC regulatory review periods' (advisory 20-061 as a footer, 'Pending All Relevant CFTC Regulatory Review Periods'). The handoff rates the 2018 launch High while U-19 rejects two 2019 days partly for carrying 'pending'. Those cannot both stand. If the boilerplate defeats LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES, TACO has no encodable launch day either and the key must be knowledge-bound at its earliest artifact; if it does not, then 2018-05-13 and 2021-09-26 are both encodable. The asymmetry in U-19 was really about two documents naming two different days, which is not the situation here: one day is named, three times, in three consecutive weekly notices, and the operator's own wiki and spec both moved to match within weeks.
encodable:
KEY globex_equity_index_taco — members ESQ (3T), NQQ (NT), RTQ (RE). tz America/Chicago throughout; every published instant is a CT clock time, so a single-tz StaticHoursProfile represents it exactly and none of U-8's cross-zone problem applies.

ERA 1 — from the January-2010 floor? NO. The key launches: first session Sunday 2018-05-13 17:00 CT, trade date Monday 2018-05-14. Before that the family did not exist, so the pre-launch state is closure (the launch-dated-venue case AGENTS.md already contemplates). Grid, all CT, from Globex Notice 2018-05-07 / SER-8124R Exhibit 1 / wiki v13:
  • Sunday 16:00 pre-open (order_entry), 17:00 open → Monday 08:30 close. Trade date Monday.
  • Monday-Thursday: 09:30 pre-open (order_entry), 10:00 open → 16:00; halt 16:00-17:00 (CME's words: 'Market Halt ... - Globex Maintenance Period'); 16:45 pre-open (order_entry); 17:00 open → 08:30 next business day close. Each such span is ONE trade date, the next business day.
  • Friday: no day session. Nothing between Friday 08:30 and Sunday 16:00.
  Trade dates fall out of the generic convention with no exception needed: every leg wraps and ends at 08:30 on its own trade date.

ERA 2 — revision row keyed to local date 2021-09-26 (the stated effective Sunday; trade date Monday 2021-09-27). Grid identical to era 1 plus a Friday day leg:
  • Friday 09:30 pre-open (order_entry), 10:00 open → 16:00 close — and the service marks this Friday 16:00 as 'closed', not 'paused' as Mon-Thu 16:00 is. There is no 16:45 pre-open / 17:00 reopen on Friday.
  • Weekend closed: Friday 16:00 → Sunday 16:00 pre-open. NO Saturday phase.
  • Sunday 16:00 pre-open, 17:00 open → Monday 08:30 close, unchanged.
  • The Monday-Thursday 16:00-17:00 halt and the Monday-Thursday evening leg are unchanged — CME expanded only the morning close line, the pre-open line and the day-session line to Monday-Friday.
  Keying the row at 2021-09-26 rather than at the first Friday it actually bites (2021-10-01, for trade date Monday 2021-10-04) is safe and is the faithful reading: between those two dates the two eras return identical answers because the Sunday and weekday grids are unchanged, so the choice is unobservable and the notice's own day should win.

WHAT AN IMPLEMENTER MUST NOT MISS — the trade date. In era 2, trade date Monday has TWO disjoint legs: Friday 10:00-16:00 CT and Sunday 17:00 → Monday 08:30 CT, separated by a ~49-hour weekend. CME states the assignment in words ('Any order submitted on Friday after 10:00am (CT) will have a next business date of Monday') and in FIX (the Taco-Friday-Scenario diagram's tag 75-TradeDate = the following Monday). The crate's generic convention — trade date = venue-local date of a containing session's final close — puts the Friday leg on FRIDAY, which is wrong. This needs a sourced trade-date exception in src/calendar/query/identity.rs, the same mechanism globex_rough_rice needed for its non-wrapping evening leg, and it is a harder instance because the two legs of one trade date are separated by a gap that is Closed (>4 h), so they must not coalesce into one session. The handoff does not flag this; it is the single hardest part of encoding TACO and it does not exist in era 1.

The service's Saturday (05:00 open, 17:00 closed) rows are withheld as a feed artifact, with the three contradicting CME prose statements cited beside the table and the anomaly recorded.   3. The CME ClearPort TACO hours. They are a distinct venue cell, ES's copy still reads Monday-Thursday while NQ's and RTY's read Monday-Friday, and ClearPort is submission-for-clearing rather than an order book — out of the crate's scope. Do not let ES's stale ClearPort cell be read as a live dispute about the Globex grid.
  4. Any BTIC-side conclusion from the 2021-09-20 notice. It says 'TACO and BTIC' and names no product codes; today only NIT/NKT show a Friday leg, while EST closes Friday 15:00 CT and ES1 Friday 16:00 CT with nothing after.
